title: Euler-Twisted Hall Products, Green Coproducts, and Quantum Groups

items.title: The Hall-normalized extended positive Borel of a loopless quiver

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For a finite loopless Q over F_q, define the symmetric Cartan matrix a_ij=2δ_ij−c_ij−c_ji and ν=√q>1. Present the extended positive Borel over Q(ν) with generators E_i,K_i^{±1}, the toral action K_iE_jK_i^{-1}=ν^{a_ij}E_j, the symmetric quantum Serre relations, and coproduct E_i↦E_i⊗K_i^{-1}+1⊗E_i, K_i↦K_i⊗K_i.

items.title: A symmetric Gaussian alternating sum vanishes in the Serre range

references.title: Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement: For m≥1 and d∈Z with 1−m≤d≤m−1 and d≡m−1 mod 2, prove Σ_{n=0}^m (−1)^n ν^(−dn) [m choose n]_ν=0.
items.strategy: Rewrite the symmetric Gaussian coefficients by the ordinary q-binomial theorem; the stated parity and bounds force a factor 1−1.

items.title: A zero Yoneda splice factors through the middle object

references.title: Barry Mitchell, Theory of Categories, Chapter VII, §§4–5
Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext

items.statement: Let E be 0→A→B→C→0 and F be 0→C→D→X→0 in an abelian category. If the Yoneda splice E∘F is zero in YExt²(X,A), then there is an extension G of X by B whose pushout along B→C is equivalent to F. Conversely every such pushout has zero splice with E.

items.title: Low-degree exact sequences for Yoneda Ext in both variables

references.title: Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: For a short exact sequence 0→A→B→C→0 and an object X, the Hom and Yoneda Ext^1 terms form the usual exact sequences in either variable, continuing through the Yoneda Ext^2 boundary.

items.title: Finite-field hereditary Hall categories

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement: A finite-field hereditary Hall category is a supplied small F_q-linear finitary abelian category in which Hom and Yoneda Ext^1 are finite-dimensional over F_q and Yoneda Ext^2 vanishes.

items.title: Finite-dimensional representations of an acyclic quiver form a hereditary finitary Hall category

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For a finite acyclic quiver Q over F_q, the category of finite-dimensional representations is a small hereditary finitary abelian category. Its simples are S_i, K_0≅Z^{Q_0}, dim_Fq Ext^1(S_i,S_j)=c_ij, and its Euler form is χ(α,β)=Σ_i α_iβ_i−Σ_{a:i→j}α_iβ_j.
items.strategy: Use the explicit length-one path resolution by finite-dimensional representable projectives, then count finite-dimensional representations and maps over the finite field.

items.title: Finite loopless quiver nilpotent representation categories are hereditary and finitary

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For a finite loopless quiver Q over F_q, the category of finite-dimensional nilpotent representations (all representations if Q is acyclic) is a small hereditary finitary abelian category; its simples are S_i, K_0≅Z^{Q_0}, and dim Ext^1(S_i,S_j)=c_ij for arrows i→j.

items.title: The hereditary Euler form is additive on the Grothendieck group

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Charles A. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra, §3.4, Yoneda Ext

items.statement: For a finite-field hereditary Hall category, χ([M],[N])=dim Hom(M,N)−dim Ext^1(M,N) is integer-valued and additive in each variable on short exact sequences, hence bilinear on K_0.
items.strategy: Apply the two low-degree Yoneda exact sequences and take alternating dimensions.

items.title: Exact-sequence counts equal endpoint automorphism counts times subobject counts

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For objects M,N,R in a small finitary abelian category, the number P^R_{M,N} of endpoint-labelled short exact sequences 0→N→R→M→0 equals |Aut(M)||Aut(N)|g^R_{M,N}.
items.strategy: Use the free endpoint-automorphism action on exact sequences; its orbits are exactly the counted subobject classes.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall algebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For a finite-field hereditary Hall category and ν=√q>0, define χ(α,β)=ν^〈α,β〉 and [M]⋆[N]=χ([M],[N])[M]*[N]; define the symmetric bicharacter ν^(〈α,β〉+〈β,α〉) used in the tensor product.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall product is well-defined

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement: The Euler-twisted Hall basis product has finite coefficients and finite support, so it extends uniquely to a bilinear product on the same direct-sum module.
items.strategy: Multiply each finite untwisted Hall coefficient and support by the fixed Euler scalar.

items.title: The Green Hall completion and coproduct

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: Define the coefficientwise completion of H⊗H and the Green coproduct Δ([R])=Σ_{M,N}ν^〈M,N〉P^R_{M,N}/|Aut(R)| [M]⊗[N], with its partial twisted tensor multiplication.

items.title: The Euler-twisted Hall product is associative and unital

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: The Euler-twisted product is an associative bilinear product with the zero-object basis class as its unit.
items.strategy: Use additivity of the Euler form to check the twist cocycle and then the untwisted Hall associativity.

items.title: Green coproduct coefficients are finite

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: For each fixed R,M,N, the coefficient of [M]⊗[N] in Δ([R]) is a finite scalar; every finite truncation has finite support where the category has finite subobjects.
items.strategy: Bound endpoint-labelled sequences by the finite product Hom(N,R)×Hom(R,M).

items.title: The Green cross–square counting identity

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement: For fixed M,N,K,L, count the common-middle crosses and the induced exact squares; the square-to-cross fiber has cardinality |Ext^1(K_2,L_1)| and its automorphism stabilizer is Hom(K_2,L_1).
items.strategy: Take kernels, images, and cokernels in each cross, then count completions by the Yoneda exact sequence and explicit automorphism stabilizers.

items.title: The extended Hall algebra and composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: Adjoin the group algebra of K_0 to the quiver Hall algebra with its symmetric Euler torus action; define the simple-generated composition subalgebra and its torus extension.

items.title: The extended Hall torus action is well-defined

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: For α∈K_0, the scaling [M]↦ν^( (α,[M]) )[M] is an algebra automorphism of the twisted Hall algebra and defines an action of the K_0 group algebra.
items.strategy: Use K_0 grading of Hall products and biadditivity of the symmetric Euler form.

items.title: The Green Hall coproduct is coassociative

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: The completed Green coproduct satisfies (Δ⊗id)Δ=(id⊗Δ)Δ coefficientwise.
items.strategy: Identify both triple coefficients with the same two-step flags and compare the bilinear Euler weights.

items.title: Products of Green coproducts converge coefficientwise

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: For any basis objects M,N, the partial twisted tensor product Δ([M])·Δ([N]) has only finitely many contributions to each coefficient [R]⊗[S].
items.strategy: Use the finite Hom sets to determine the relevant image subobjects in any contributing diagram.

items.title: Green’s coproduct is an algebra map into the twisted tensor completion

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Matthew B. Young, Degenerate versions of Green’s theorem for Hall modules, arXiv:1810.08238v2

items.statement: For a hereditary finitary abelian category, the Green coproduct is coassociative and multiplicative into the coefficientwise completion when the tensor multiplication is twisted by the symmetric Euler bicharacter.
items.strategy: Expand both sides on basis elements, reduce coefficients to the cross-square count, and verify coefficientwise convergence.

items.title: The Green Hall pairing is nondegenerate and adjoint to product and coproduct

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: The diagonal form ([M],[N])=δ_[M],[N]/|Aut(M)| is nondegenerate over Q(ν) and satisfies ([M]⋆[N],[R])=([M]⊗[N],Δ([R])).
items.strategy: Evaluate both pairings on basis elements and use the exact-sequence normalization.

items.title: The extended Green coproduct is an algebra map

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: With group-like torus elements and the stated Euler cross-relations, the extended Green coproduct is multiplicative for the ordinary tensor product algebra.
items.strategy: Check the group-like and Hall generators and use the torus action to convert the twisted tensor factor into the extended tensor product.

items.title: The extended Green and repository Drinfeld–Jimbo coproduct conventions agree on simple generators

references.title: Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: For a vertex simple S_i, the DJ-compatible extended Green coproduct has Δ₋([S_i])=[S_i]⊗k_i^{-1}+1⊗[S_i], exactly matching the repository Drinfeld–Jimbo coproduct on E_i. The alternative Hall convention Δ₊([S_i])=[S_i]⊗1+k_i⊗[S_i] is kept distinct.
items.strategy: Evaluate the extended Green formula on a simple object and compare the two generator coproducts term by term.

items.title: The Ringel assignment is a bialgebra homomorphism onto the extended composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement: The assignment E_i↦[S_i], K_i↦k_i respects the symmetric Cartan and quantum Serre relations and the extended Green coproduct Δ₋; its image is the subalgebra generated by the simple classes and torus. The proof is drafted for finite loopless Q, with the cyclic nilpotent-category hereditary supplier unresolved.
items.strategy: Check the symmetric Cartan action, count simple filtrations to verify every Serre coefficient, and compare the group-like coproduct formulas.

items.title: The Ringel map embeds the extended positive Borel and is full Hall exactly in finite Dynkin type

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement: For finite loopless Q over F_q (using finite-dimensional nilpotent representations when Q has oriented cycles), the Ringel map from the extended positive Borel embeds into the extended Hall algebra with image the torus extension of the composition subalgebra; the positive half maps onto the full Hall algebra exactly when the underlying graph is finite Dynkin.

title: Euler-Twisted Hall Products, Green Coproducts, and Quantum Groups: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The Kronecker Hall algebra strictly contains its composition subalgebra

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2

items.statement: The assertion that every loopless-quiver Hall algebra is generated by its simple classes is false: for the two-arrow Kronecker quiver, the degree (1,1) Hall component has q+2 basis classes while the composition component has dimension at most 2.
items.strategy: Classify dimension-(1,1) representations by a pair of arrow scalars modulo endpoint rescaling and count the two simple-generator words.

items.title: A one-vertex Green coproduct and twisted Hall square

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)

items.statement: For the one-vertex zero-arrow quiver over F_q, compute [S]⋆[S]=ν(q+1)[S⊕S] and Δ([S⊕S]) including the mixed coefficient ν^(−1).
items.strategy: Count the lines in F_q^2 and the endpoint-labelled exact sequences with middle F_q^2.

items.title: The A2 Hall products and their quantum Serre relation

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, The Hall Algebra Approach to Quantum Groups, E.L.A.M. Lectures (1993)
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591

items.statement: For the one-arrow quiver 1→2, compute the two simple products and verify the rank-two ν-Serre relation in degree (2,1).
items.strategy: Classify the two representation isoclasses in the relevant dimension vectors and count the required subobjects.
